title: Reusable MCP verification ladder -- initialize alone is not sufficient proof
summary: An 8-level ladder for verifying an MCP server is genuinely operational: CONFIGURATION_PRESENT, PROCESS_STARTS, INITIALIZE_SUCCEEDS, TOOLS_CAPABILITY_DECLARED, TOOLS_LIST_SUCCEEDS, EXPECTED_TOOL_CATALOG_APPEARS, REAL_READ_ONLY_TOOL_CALL_SUCCEEDS, CLAUDE_CLIENT_EXPOSES_AND_INVOKES. Proven across five MCP servers in this mission. Declaring a server 'operational' at Level 1 or 2 alone is a known failure pattern.
retrievalQuestions: What is the correct sequence of steps to verify a Claude Code MCP server is actually operational?
Is it sufficient to prove an MCP server is working if its initialize call succeeds?
What are the 8 levels of the MCP verification ladder used in the estate remediation mission?

futureAgentInstructions.whenThisAppears: A future agent needs to confirm whether a Claude Code MCP server (governed or estate) is genuinely operational, not just configured
runPreflight: a raw initialize -> notifications/initialized -> tools/list -> tools/call probe
doNot: Declare an MCP server 'operational' based on Level 1 (process starts) or Level 2 (initialize succeeds) alone
Skip the real read-only tools/call step (Level 6) when claiming a server is verified live
proveBeforeClaiming: A real tools/call against a safe, read-only tool returned a successful, expected result
The tool catalog returned by tools/list matches what the server's own source code declares
